release.target: The Local Connect bundle download for Linux and Windows. Each app may also be released on its own.

automate_scope.decision: in the first release: the three cross-app automations
automate_scope.note: The bundle is not ready for release until each automation is demonstrated installed on Linux and Windows, together with every automated check its task names.

issue_gate.note: Every open issue in this milestone blocks the affected app release; the bundle gate includes all four repositories. Issues explain blockers but never count as evidence.

invoice-processor.note_python: Verification interpreter. uv otherwise picks the newest installed CPython, and a verdict must be comparable across revisions; the app declares >=3.13 and 3.13 is what its development and the earlier verified runs used.

ew.ci.windows_package.note: Builds the NSIS installer, verifies engine process-tree lifecycle, re-runs the packaged engine smoke. A build artifact, not a release.

ds.ci.rust.note: fmt, test all targets/features, clippy on ubuntu-24.04.

ds.cargo.lib.note: Needs frontend build first; ~10 min cold. Opt in with --heavy.

ip.pytest.all.note: Whole suite. tests/test_shell.py shells out to a node static check and needs desktop/node_modules.

xapp.accept_ew_to_ip.note: The acceptance script drives the exact extracted Email Watcher engine API and Invoice Processor provider over loopback, with the exact contracts keyring and a stand-in model, inside an isolated HOME with its own XDG roots. The collector's installed Connect entitlement is pre-checked (structure and validity window only), staged into that HOME, and removed on every exit path. A zero exit passes only with the complete machine-readable nine-check proof. All three revisions are recorded. No GPU.

xapp.accept_ew_to_ds.note: Builds the exact Document Summarizer tree with the exact contracts keyring, then drives it through Email Watcher's real cross-process PDF proof with a stand-in model and software rendering. All three revisions are recorded. No GPU.

manual.ip_removal_test.note: scripts/removal_test.py: install the .deb, drive the packaged Email Watcher through not-installed / installed / removed. Needs sudo dpkg; a person runs it and records the transcript.

manual.ew_live_calendar.note: Live Microsoft consent, proposal and confirmed write against a real tenant, on the installed app. Recorded in docs/CONTRACTS.md acceptance appendix.

inspect.ew_queue_scheduler.note: Exact-revision discovery hints only. Behavioral evidence is still required.

manual.auto_pdf_summary_linux.note: With the installed Linux apps and a licence granting connect.automations: define a rule once (this sender, any PDF). A matching mail's PDF is summarized with no click and the notification carries the summary; at least one matching mail carries a scanned PDF with no text layer, summarized through OCR; a non-matching mail is not handed over.

manual.auto_invoice_digest_linux.note: With the installed Linux apps and a licence granting connect.automations: define a vendor-and-bill rule. Each matching bill is filed into the ledger with no click; at least one is a scanned PDF with no text layer, filed through OCR; a busy provider leaves a bill queued and it then completes; the scheduled digest lists what arrived and what is due; nothing is paid.

manual.bundle_download_linux.note: On Linux: One bundle download installs the three apps and the shared runtime (the model host and the OCR provider), with exactly one model copy and no configuration. Each app's first launch uses that one server: one model file on disk, one server process. Document Summarizer and Invoice Processor each read a scanned PDF with no text layer.

manual.bundle_download_windows.note: On Windows: One bundle download installs the three apps and the shared runtime (the model host and the OCR provider), with exactly one model copy and no configuration. Each app's first launch uses that one server: one model file on disk, one server process. Document Summarizer and Invoice Processor each read a scanned PDF with no text layer.

manual.bundle_licence_online_linux.note: On Linux: The apps obtain and keep a valid licence online as the licensing model in invoice-processor#94 (private) specifies, from first launch onward, without user configuration. All three apps verify it locally under entitlement v1 (connect.capability_exchange, connect.automations), and the handoffs and automations are active in all three.

manual.bundle_licence_online_windows.note: On Windows: The apps obtain and keep a valid licence online as the licensing model in invoice-processor#94 (private) specifies, from first launch onward, without user configuration. All three apps verify it locally under entitlement v1 (connect.capability_exchange, connect.automations), and the handoffs and automations are active in all three.

manual.bundle_without_licence_linux.note: On Linux: With no valid licence (expired or absent): each app's standalone flow and all user data keep working, and Document Summarizer and Invoice Processor still read a scanned PDF with no text layer. One-click handoffs and the automations stop, each showing a plain message. Importing a hand-signed offline licence restores them without going online.

manual.bundle_without_licence_windows.note: On Windows: With no valid licence (expired or absent): each app's standalone flow and all user data keep working, and Document Summarizer and Invoice Processor still read a scanned PDF with no text layer. One-click handoffs and the automations stop, each showing a plain message. Importing a hand-signed offline licence restores them without going online.

manual.bundle_privacy_linux.note: On Linux: While the automation demonstrations (including a scan) and the online licence behaviour run, every outbound connection of the installed apps, model host and OCR provider is recorded. Every destination is one the privacy promise in invoice-processor#94 (private) allows, and no request carries document content. The artifact is the capture and its destination summary.

manual.bundle_privacy_windows.note: On Windows: While the automation demonstrations (including a scan) and the online licence behaviour run, every outbound connection of the installed apps, model host and OCR provider is recorded. Every destination is one the privacy promise in invoice-processor#94 (private) allows, and no request carries document content. The artifact is the capture and its destination summary.

tasks.title: I hear about the mail that matters, without checking
tasks.promise: Watch chosen senders on Gmail, Microsoft 365, or any IMAP mailbox; read each new message with a local model; tell me what it is, how urgent, and what it asks; notify me on the desktop and optionally my phone.
tasks.human_involvement: You pick the senders and connect the mailbox once. Phone alerts are off until you set a topic.

conditions.proves: All three mail adapters connect and behave read-only in tests.
Desktop and ntfy channels deliver independently; ntfy only with a topic.
Whole suite green on a GitHub Linux runner.
Locking, config and Windows Connect placement tests pass on a Windows runner.

tasks.title: A meeting request in my mail becomes a calendar event I approve
tasks.promise: Without a click, spot a meeting request in watched mail, extract only times traceable to exact quotes, check my calendar, propose a slot, and — only after I confirm one specific proposal — create the event, telling me first who will receive invitations.
tasks.human_involvement: Confirmation is required before anything is written. The automation stops on ambiguous mail and waits for review. Microsoft 365 only.

conditions.proves: Extracted times must trace to source quotes; unsupported dates/zones are dropped.
Runs only with both licence features; reaches a durable confirmation preview; reviewable when no common time.
Event creation is idempotent per transaction and classifies ambiguous outcomes.
A person observed consent, proposal and a confirmed write against a real tenant.
A person observed consent, proposal and a confirmed write against a real tenant on the installed Windows app.

tasks.title: A PDF becomes a summary I can check against the page
tasks.promise: Summarize a text PDF in General, Story or Contract mode; every claim cites an exact source quote and is marked supported, unsupported or ambiguous; warn me when coverage falls short; never modify the file.
tasks.human_involvement: Choose the PDF. Read the warnings. The app suggests a mode; you can override it.

conditions.proves: All targets and features tested, fmt and clippy clean, on a GitHub Linux runner.
Library tests pass on this machine at the exact revision (heavy; opt-in).

tasks.title: A vendor bill is read into a ledger I can audit
tasks.promise: Extract vendor, number, dates, line items and totals with every value tied to a span on the page; withhold what cannot be verified; catch duplicates; track received → reviewed → paid; keep records across uninstall.
tasks.human_involvement: You review each entry before it can be paid. Unresolved duplicates block review.

conditions.proves: The whole Invoice Processor test suite passes at the current revision.
Unknown spans, non-verbatim values and unknown currency are withheld, never guessed.
State machine, duplicate derivation and resolution, purge boundaries.
Uninstall touches nothing under the data directory; nothing claims a signature.

tasks.title: One click summarizes the PDF in my mail
tasks.promise: With both apps installed and licensed, a Summarize action appears on a PDF attachment inside Email Watcher; the file alone is handed over loopback; the cited summary comes back and stays with the message.
tasks.human_involvement: You click. Requires the licence in both apps.

conditions.proves: The exact consumer, provider, and contract revisions complete the real loopback PDF handoff with a stand-in model.
Summarize handoff persists results, survives provider failure, never masquerades failure as success.
Consumer suite green on GitHub.

tasks.title: An emailed bill appears in my ledger
tasks.promise: With both apps installed and licensed, a Read invoice action appears on a bill inside Email Watcher; the bill is handed to Invoice Processor over loopback; it lands in the ledger through the same path as a hand-opened file, entry marked received, waiting for review.
tasks.human_involvement: You click, and you review the entry before it can be paid. A second bill may wait durably while the provider is busy.

conditions.proves: A Connect job produces a real ledger entry through Ledger.ingest with duplicate detection; the provider writes no ledger table itself.
Generic invoke requires explicit provider and confirmation, persists first, reconciles lost acks.
Exact extracted Email Watcher and Invoice Processor code runs end to end over loopback with the exact contracts keyring, a stand-in model, and all three revisions recorded.
A PROVIDER_BUSY job is held durably and resubmitted with the same identity when pumped.
Packaged apps discover each other, and removal leaves the ledger and the other app untouched.

tasks.title: A PDF from a vendor is summarized before I open it
tasks.promise: A rule I define — this sender, any PDF — hands the file to Document Summarizer without a click and notifies me with the summary in hand.
tasks.human_involvement: You define the rule once; afterward no click is part of the promised flow.

conditions.proves: A person can define a sender-and-attachment rule for this flow.
On the installed Linux apps, a rule the person defined once summarizes a matching mail's PDF with no click, including a scanned PDF read through OCR, and leaves a non-matching mail alone.
On the installed Windows apps, a rule the person defined once summarizes a matching mail's PDF with no click, including a scanned PDF read through OCR, and leaves a non-matching mail alone.

tasks.title: Bills file themselves and I get a digest
tasks.promise: A rule — this vendor, a PDF that looks like a bill — routes each arrival into the ledger without a click, batches survive a busy provider, and a scheduled digest tells me what arrived and what is due.
tasks.human_involvement: You define the routing and digest rule; review before payment stays with you.

conditions.proves: A person can define a vendor-and-invoice rule for this flow.
The desktop schedules Connect queue pumping without a manual click.

On the installed Linux apps, a vendor-and-bill rule files each matching bill with no click, including a scanned PDF read through OCR, survives a busy provider, and a scheduled digest lists what arrived and what is due.

On the installed Windows apps, a vendor-and-bill rule files each matching bill with no click, including a scanned PDF read through OCR, survives a busy provider, and a scheduled digest lists what arrived and what is due.
